content.thinking: Confirmed the race is real: watermarks count appends at open time rather than commit, so an in-flight appender with ID ≤ watermark can commit after block-building, slip past the eviction guard, and get evicted with its sample lost from both the block and the WAL. I'm rating it medium since it requires a concurrent append during compaction, which the code already discourages—and noting the head appender code wasn't available to verify directly, so I relied on upstream Prometheus behavior.

input.reason: The watermark counts appenders that haven't committed yet. isolation.lastAppendID() returns the highest ID handed out (newAppendID increments it when an appender opens), while the block writer's iso.State() marks open IDs as incomplete and leaves their samples out. If an appender opened before the watermark (ID N ≤ watermark) commits after the block snapshot, its ID lands in s.txs. hasAppendIDAbove(s, watermark) then returns false, so with a sample timestamp ≤ maxt the series is evicted and a WAL expiry is written. The sample is lost from the head, the block and WAL replay. The new comment's 'guaranteed' claim is therefore false and the new guard misses this case.
